g.text: The full two-sided Yoneda evaluation
Actual functor cores · every middle identity retained
X_F(x;y) = ⊕ C(Fb₀,y) ⊗ (sB)ʳ ⊗ B(x,bᵣ)
(k ; w ; l) w = sb₁ | ⋯ | sbᵣ
q(k ; w ; l) = (−1)ᵗ k τ_F(w | sl)
The final coefficient l becomes the last bar letter.
Extra-unit insertion, followed by normalization
D h_raw + h_raw D = 1 − s q
Π = 1 − s q h′ = h_raw Π h = h′ D h′
D h + h D = Π h² = 0
No identity word was deleted to obtain h² = 0.
An ordinary identity from a genuine higher core
V = k e⁰ ⊕ k f⁻¹ ⊕ k y⁰ d(f) = y
q_Φ(1 ; sE_ef | sE_yf ; E_ye) = 1_V
|sE_ef| = |sE_yf| = 0: the evaluation sign is plus.
For F = exp[b,H_fun], retain the sign on every word.
Omitting (−1)ᵗ gives (d q̃ − q̃ D)(1 ; sE_fe ; E_ef)
A chain equation detects the sign before taking cohomology.
Proof and exact signs: Theorem 23. Matrix calculations: Exercise 23.
